seo.title: How to Add Your Business to Apple Maps
seo.meta_description: How to add or claim a business location on Apple Maps with Apple Business, verify it by phone and keep hours accurate, for Anaheim and Orange County.

h1: How to Add Your Business to Apple Maps and Keep It Accurate
answer: To add your business to Apple Maps, sign in to Apple Business, add a single location, place the pin on the right building, then enter your category, status, phone, website and hours. If the location already exists, you may be able to verify it with a phone call. Anaheim and Orange County businesses should also watch for Apple's emails about changes customers report.
key_takeaways: Place the pin over the correct building.
Existing locations may verify by phone.
You can request a transfer if someone else manages it.
Apple emails you when it edits name, status or hours.

sections.heading: Apple Business Connect is now Apple Business
sections.body_html: Apple's guide states that Apple Business Connect is now Apple Business, which combines what was previously in Apple Business Manager, Apple Business Essentials and Apple Business Connect into one offering. If you used Apple Business Connect before, you can sign in to Apple Business with the same personal Apple Account.

sections.heading: Add a single location
sections.body_html: Apple's guide says to enter the location's name, find and select it, and if the marker is over the wrong building, drag the map or enter coordinates. Switching to Hybrid or Satellite view helps you see your entrance.

sections.heading: Enter the details
sections.body_html:
• Default language and display name.
  • Primary category; Apple updates categories regularly, so check for better matches later.
  • Status: Open or Opening Soon, with an opening date up to six months away.
  • Phone number and an optional website; a Facebook, Instagram or TikTok page can also be used.
  • Hours of operation.
  • The brand the location belongs to.

sections.heading: Verify by phone
sections.body_html: Apple says phone verification may be available if the location already exists on Maps. Apple calls the number it has on record, and you enter the four-digit code. If you don't recognize the number, contact Apple Business support.

sections.heading: If someone else manages it
sections.body_html: If the location is already managed by another organization, Apple lets you request a transfer from Brands, Locations, Request Transfer, with supporting documents such as a business license or utility bill. Apple says the review can take up to five business days.

sections.heading: Brands and locations
sections.body_html: Apple's guide explains that every location is associated with a brand. Brand details, such as name, logo and cover photo, cascade to the brand's locations, though each location can have its own cover photo. Whether you have one location or a thousand, each can be managed separately.

sections.heading: Customer reports
sections.body_html: Apple says that if your place card shows you as open and a customer finds you closed, they can report it from the place card. Apple reviews reports and may edit your place card, then emails your administrators when it changes your name, status or hours.

sections.heading: Accept or contest Apple's changes
sections.body_html: From Brands, Locations, select a location with the status Updates Available, review the alert and select Looks Good if correct. If not, edit the status, hours or name; name changes go to Apple for review, which can take up to five business days.

sections.heading: Keep hours current
sections.body_html: Wrong hours are the most common reason customers report a place. Update hours for holidays and special events in Apple Business as well as on Google, your website and other listings.

sections.heading: Common mistakes
sections.body_html:
• Leaving the pin on the wrong building or parking lot.
  • Using a website that doesn't match the business name.
  • Ignoring Apple's change emails.
  • Creating a duplicate instead of requesting a transfer.
  • Forgetting holiday hours on Apple Maps.

sections.heading: Questions owners ask us
sections.body_html: Owners often ask why their business shows the wrong location on Apple Maps. Usually the pin was placed from an old address or a nearby building; adding or claiming the location lets you move it, using satellite view to place it on your entrance. Another question is whether service-area businesses can use Apple Maps. Apple's guide focuses on physical locations, so make sure the address you add is one customers can actually visit. Owners also ask how to handle a move. Update the address, check the pin and hours, then update Google, your website and directories the same day so customers don't get mixed messages.

sections.heading: Checklist
sections.body_html:
• Location added or claimed.
  • Pin on the correct building.
  • Category, phone, website and hours set.
  • Verification completed.
  • Apple emails reach your inbox.
  • Holiday hours updated.

sections.heading: An example
sections.body_html: Imagine a bakery in Orange whose Apple Maps pin sits on the shop next door. The owner adds the location in Apple Business, switches to Satellite view to drag the pin onto the bakery's entrance, enters the hours and phone number, and verifies with a phone call to the number Apple has on record. Customers following Apple Maps now arrive at the right door.

sections.heading: How this fits your local plan
sections.body_html: Treat this as part of a routine rather than a one-off fix. Local visibility in Anaheim and the rest of Orange County comes from many small, accurate signals adding up: a verified profile, consistent listings, useful service pages, real photos and a flow of honest reviews. Google is open that relevance, distance and popularity drive local results. You cannot change distance, but you can make sure Google and AI assistants understand exactly what you do and see evidence that customers value it. Put a monthly reminder in the calendar to check the profile, read new reviews and update anything that has changed.

sections.heading: What to do this week
sections.body_html:
1. Search for your business in Apple Maps.
  2. Add or claim it in Apple Business.
  3. Check the pin and hours.
  4. Whitelist apple.com emails.

sections.heading: When to get help
sections.body_html: You do not need an agency for every step here; Google documents most of it clearly. Consider outside help when the work is urgent and unfamiliar, when you manage several locations, or when the same issue returns after you fix it. Ask any provider to show you the specific guideline or documentation behind each recommendation, to keep you as the owner of your accounts and to report results in calls, bookings and leads rather than vanity numbers. That is how Chimera works with Orange County businesses from our base in Anaheim.

sections.heading: A monthly accuracy check
sections.body_html: Apple Maps and Google Maps are separate systems, so a change on one doesn't update the other. Once a month, open your business in Apple Maps on an iPhone as a customer would. Check that the pin sits on your entrance, the hours match your door sign, the phone number rings through and the website link opens. Compare everything with your Google Business Profile and website. Look in Apple Business for any location showing Updates Available, and read Apple's emails rather than filtering them. If you've changed anything in the last month, such as holiday hours or a new phone system, confirm it's reflected on Apple Maps too. Ten minutes a month prevents the most common problem: a customer driving to a closed business because one map was out of date.

sections.heading: The short version
sections.body_html: Add or claim your location in Apple Business, place the pin correctly, complete every detail, and respond to Apple's change emails. Chimera, based in Anaheim, keeps Apple Maps listings accurate for Orange County businesses.
